strings.d1.s0.name: Ocean Drive Art Deco
strings.d1.s0.tips: Pastel Art Deco hotels; best in morning light. Look out for the Versace mansion (Casa Casuarina).
strings.d1.s1.name: South Beach
strings.d1.s1.tips: White sand and lifeguard huts; 10th Street is the famous stretch. Mornings are calm and windless.
strings.d1.s2.name: Puerto Sagua Restaurant
strings.d1.s2.tips: A Cuban diner since 1962; try the ropa vieja (shredded beef stew) and café con leche in South Beach.
strings.d1.s3.name: Española Way
strings.d1.s4.name: South Pointe Park
strings.d1.s4.tips: A park and pier at the tip of the island; watch ships pass and catch the sunset.
strings.d1.b0.name: Joe's Stone Crab
strings.d1.b0.tips: Serving stone crab since 1913 (October to May); in South Pointe.
strings.d1.b1.name: Wolfsonian FIU
strings.d1.b1.tips: A design museum focused on Art Deco; a good rainy-day option.
strings.d2.s0.name: Wynwood Walls
strings.d2.s0.tips: The world's best-known street art garden. Buy tickets online; the surrounding streets are free.
strings.d2.s1.name: Wynwood Street Art Tour
strings.d2.s1.tips: Murals along NW 2nd Ave, plus galleries.
strings.d2.s2.name: Coyo Taco Wynwood
strings.d2.s2.tips: Mexican street tacos, with a hidden bar in the back room.
strings.d2.s3.name: Design District
strings.d2.s3.tips: Luxury shops and public art, including the Buckminster Fuller dome; ICA Miami is free.
strings.d2.s4.name: Institute of Contemporary Art Miami
strings.d2.s4.tips: Free contemporary art in the Design District.
strings.d2.b0.name: Zak the Baker Wynwood
strings.d2.b0.tips: An award-winning sourdough bakery; an alternative to tacos.
strings.d2.b1.name: Pérez Art Museum Miami
strings.d2.b1.tips: A waterfront museum with hanging gardens.
strings.d3.s0.name: Calle Ocho
strings.d3.s0.tips: SW 8th Street: rooster statues, cigar shops and salsa.
strings.d3.s1.name: Domino Park Máximo Gómez
strings.d3.s1.tips: A park where older locals play dominoes; ask permission before taking photos.
strings.d3.s2.name: Ball & Chain
strings.d3.s2.tips: A salsa club dating from 1935; come at lunchtime for a mojito and empanada, with live music.
strings.d3.s3.name: Versailles Restaurant
strings.d3.s3.tips: The world's best-known Cuban restaurant (1971); get a cafecito from the ventanita (walk-up window), plus croquetas and vaca frita (fried shredded beef).
strings.d3.s4.name: Azucar Ice Cream
strings.d3.s4.tips: Cuban ice cream; try the Abuela María flavour.
strings.d3.b0.name: El Pub Restaurant
strings.d3.b0.tips: Cuban sandwich; a good choice if the Versailles queue is long.
strings.d3.b1.name: Cubaocho Museum
strings.d3.b1.tips: Cuban art and a rum bar; an alternative to Ball & Chain.
strings.d4.s0.name: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
strings.d4.s0.tips: A 1916 Italian villa with bayfront gardens; cooler in the morning, closed on Tuesdays.
strings.d4.s1.name: Coconut Grove
strings.d4.s1.tips: A neighbourhood of banyan trees, with CocoWalk.
strings.d4.s2.name: GreenStreet Cafe
strings.d4.s2.tips: A Coconut Grove brunch classic with a terrace.
strings.d4.s3.name: Crandon Park
strings.d4.s3.tips: Reach the island over the Rickenbacker Causeway; shallow water and palm trees. Entry is 7 USD per car.
strings.d4.s4.name: Bill Baggs Cape Florida Lighthouse
strings.d4.s4.tips: A lighthouse and beach; good for sunset.
strings.d4.b0.name: Rusty Pelican Key Biscayne
strings.d4.b0.tips: Seafood with views over the bay.
strings.d4.b1.name: Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden
strings.d4.b1.tips: A tropical garden; an alternative to the beach.
strings.d5.s0.name: Everglades Safari Park
strings.d5.s0.tips: 45 minutes from Miami (by car or tour). Take an airboat ride (about 42 USD) past alligators and sawgrass; cooler in the morning.
strings.d5.s1.name: Shark Valley Tram
strings.d5.s1.tips: A 24 km tram or bike ride in the national park, with an observation tower and alligators along the way.
strings.d5.s2.name: Robert Is Here Fruit Stand
strings.d5.s2.tips: A tropical fruit stand in Homestead; try the key lime milkshake.
strings.d5.s3.name: Coral Castle
strings.d5.s3.tips: A castle of coral rock carved by one man, in Homestead.
strings.d5.b0.name: Everglades Holiday Park
strings.d5.b1.name: Homestead Cuban Restaurant
strings.d6.s0.name: Bayside Marketplace
strings.d6.s0.tips: A waterfront market; boat tours depart from here.
strings.d6.s1.name: Biscayne Bay Boat Tour
strings.d6.s1.tips: Millionaires' islands and the city skyline; 90 minutes.
strings.d6.s2.name: Brickell City Centre
strings.d6.s2.tips: A shopping centre in the financial district; air-conditioned.
strings.d6.s3.name: La Mar by Gastón Acurio
strings.d6.s3.tips: Peruvian cuisine at the Mandarin Oriental; ceviche with views over the bay.
strings.d6.s4.name: Brickell Key Walkway
strings.d6.s4.tips: A waterfront path around the island; sunset and skyscrapers.
strings.d6.b0.name: CVI.CHE 105 Downtown
strings.d6.b0.tips: Peruvian ceviche at a more affordable price.
strings.d6.b1.name: Phillip and Patricia Frost Museum of Science
strings.d6.b1.tips: An aquarium and planetarium; a good rainy-day option.
strings.d7.s0.name: Lincoln Road Mall
strings.d7.s0.tips: A pedestrian shopping street; coffee and last-minute souvenirs.
strings.d7.s1.name: Miami Beach Boardwalk
strings.d7.s1.tips: A wooden seafront path from 21st to 46th Street; your last look at the sea.
strings.d7.s2.name: Yardbird Southern Table
strings.d7.s2.tips: Southern cooking: fried chicken and waffles for a farewell meal.
strings.d7.s3.name: Miami International Airport Metrorail
strings.d7.s3.tips: 20 minutes to the airport; time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: La Sandwicherie Miami Beach
strings.d7.b0.tips: French-style sandwiches for a quick farewell bite.
strings.d7.b1.name: Bass Museum of Art
strings.d7.b1.tips: Miami Beach's art museum; an alternative to the boardwalk.
strings.note0: Miami is hard without a car: rent one for the Everglades and Key Biscayne, and use Uber or Lyft for South Beach, Wynwood and Little Havana. Metromover is free.
strings.note1: December to April is ideal (24°C, dry). March brings spring break crowds, Art Basel is in December, and stone crab season runs October to May.
strings.note2: Cuban coffee (cafecito) from a ventanita costs 2 USD; Cuban sandwiches, croquetas and ropa vieja in Little Havana cost 15-25 USD.
strings.note3: Tip 18-20% (some places add it to the bill automatically, so don't pay twice); beach loungers cost 30-50 USD.
strings.note4: Sunscreen and water are essential; UV is very high at midday.
strings.note5: Book Everglades airboat tours 2-3 days ahead; alligators are most active in the morning.
